about.title: Napa Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing someone suddenly changes everything, and the paperwork that follows can feel impossible to face. In Napa, public records show 3 traffic deaths in 2025 alongside 253 injury collisions, a small number on paper and an enormous one for each family behind it. The city's collision reports cluster most heavily along Jefferson Street, Route 29, Soscol Avenue and 1st Street. A wrongful death claim is a civil matter, separate from anything the Napa County District Attorney may pursue, and it exists so surviving family members can recover funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have provided, and compensation for the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. California limits who can bring the claim, starting with a spouse or domestic partner and children, and it sets a two-year deadline from the date of death, shorter if a public agency is involved. LawProactive is a free service. We listen, then connect you with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California gives standing first to a spouse or domestic partner and children, then to certain dependents and heirs. The attorney we connect you with can sort out where your family stands before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines handled early

items.question: My relative died in a crash on Route 29 near Napa. Does a criminal case replace a civil claim?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action, and it can move forward whether or not Napa County prosecutors file charges. The civil case focuses on your family's losses, such as funeral costs, lost support and the loss of companionship and guidance. An attorney can explain how the two processes may run side by side.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California law puts the surviving spouse or domestic partner and children first in line. If none exist, certain dependents and heirs may be eligible instead. Because the rules can get complicated with blended families, it helps to have an attorney review your specific situation.

items.question: How long do we have to act after a death in Napa?
items.answer: In most cases the deadline is two years from the date of death. If a city, county or state agency may share responsibility, a government claim must be filed much sooner, often within six months. Reaching out early gives the attorney time to gather records before those windows close.
